name: What's the difference between an attached and a detached in-law suite?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between an attached and a detached in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached in-law suite shares one or more walls with the primary residence, often built as an extension or by converting existing space like a garage. Detached in-law suites are separate, standalone structures on the property, providing maximum privacy and often feeling like a small independent home. Attached suites typically have lower construction costs due to shared utilities and foundations, while detached units offer more design flexibility and a greater sense of autonomy for occupants. Your choice depends on property layout, budget, and desired level of privacy.
acceptedAnswer.description: Attached suites share walls with the main house, costing less, while detached suites are standalone structures offering greater privacy and design flexibility.
